fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is the sole selectable candidate, but even a surviving affine NAND map would establish only a local E6 shell labeling. COPY, emitted gluing, unrestricted min-plus closure, malformed outside states, and lambda/mu >= 65/64 would remain unproved and must not be inferred from this experiment.

Proposal 2 is not implementation-ready: the combined NAND/COPY quadratic, seam equations, weight domain, and transfer-state partition are unspecified. Enumeration of [-3,3]^3 without a derived coercive bound is not an all-lattice certificate, and merely realizing a Delaunay NAND simplex does not address G28/G32/G37 strict recursive growth.

Proposal 3 is internally reversed: deep-hole cosets maximize coset-leader energy, so malformed cosets cannot all have larger leader energy than legal deep-hole cosets. Moreover, a linear syndrome construction remains exposed to G13 honest-affine collisions unless an enlarged encoding is explicitly shown to separate them.

Proposal 4 supplies no frozen tile, metric, port map, or finite transfer search and gives no mechanism forcing nonadditive depth-two growth. Ideal residues and quotient carries remain linear, so G13 collisions and free-kernel representatives must be tested rather than declared covered; small-field enumeration cannot establish a uniform arithmetic theorem.

Proposal 5 is killed structurally. Minimizing a submodular graph-cut function over auxiliaries preserves submodularity on the ports, whose minimizers are closed under coordinatewise union and intersection; NAND legal states 011 and 101 have false union 111, so exactly the four NAND words cannot be its ground-state set.

Proposal 6 does not define a finite complete boundary state space: integral boundary classes are generally infinite, and SNF describes divisibility rather than all Euclidean minimum-filling energies. Dual calibrations for selected classes do not exclude G19 signed-cycle cancellation or prove lambda>mu under gluing.
evidence: The supplied E6 verifier exactly certifies that the 27 Gosset vertices are all lattice points through squared radius 4/3. This makes coefficient-unbounded affine classification on that fixed shell a genuine bounded discriminator for the current Voronoi frontier.

The same verifier rejects only rows in {-1,0,1}^6; it provides no evidence against arbitrary rational affine coefficients. Seven affinely independent shell vertices determine every rational affine row, so enumerating their binary values closes that gap without coefficient bounds.

G13 verifies an exact honest-affine collision defeating every compatible raw linear syndrome, and G15 shows that collision lifting through a hierarchy with zero residual. Coding and ideal-quotient proposals therefore need an explicit enlarged-state escape, not a scope disclaimer.

G28, G32, and G37 independently show that finite local separation or favorable one-copy cost does not imply strict recursive growth: tested adverse costs were submultiplicative or exactly additive. No proposal except the E6 classification offers a presently frozen, exhaustive experiment justified by existing verifier data.

The D4 verifier results are finite family rejections only and leave unrelated nonseparable cells open. They do not obstruct the coefficient-unbounded E6 test, while they forbid promoting any local shell success to a general Voronoi theorem.
